I have Lakka OS (the partner OS of the RetroArch emulation project) installed on a HP Stream mini PC. It's about the size of a tupperware container and has two USB ports in the front (more in the back) that are perfect for plugging controllers into and playing on. It boots right into Lakka so I don't need a keyboard or mouse.
I've never heard of this. What is it exactly?

RetroArch is emulation software (emulates NES, SNES, Megadrive, N64, etc) that allows you to play old video game ROMs on your PC (Windows, Linux, Android). Lakka started as an unofficial project to write an OS and front-end UI for RetroArch so that you can install Lakka onto a mini-PC or RaspberryPI and boot directly to it with a nice looking front-end. Eventually the project got enough traction that the project leads of Lakka and RetroArch are working together officially, and the front-end from Lakka was adopted back into RetroArch on other platforms.

Here's a short demo of the Lakka UI (it's an older version): http://www.lakka.tv/videos/menump4.mp4

Here's the Lakka project page: http://www.lakka.tv/

And here's the RetroArch project page: http://www.libretro.com/
